gen-gf-bbh-hegarty-fs-literata: Pinched-neck letters, spaced like fence posts. Literata, a text serif, answers with sturdy thin lines and open curves, so the heading's closed shapes and the body's open ones keep trading places.
gen-gf-belanosima-fs-literata: Stout, uniform strokes with no fuss. Belanosima keeps one fixed nib width from top to baseline, while Literata, a text serif, thins its curves slightly at the tops, and that gap is the whole charm.
gen-gf-belleza-fs-literata: Knotted-close letters with an inviting, rounded face. Belleza handles the opening statement with moderate stroke swings, while Literata, a text serif, does the steady work of carrying sentences with its sturdy thin and thick lines.
gen-gf-bentham-fs-bespoke-sans: Editorial through and through. Bentham's hairlines and bold stems swing hard, and Bespoke Sans stays low in contrast, with generous space at its curve ends, so paragraphs read smoothly beneath it.
gen-gf-cabin-sketch-roboto-slab: Bold, marker-drawn letters, tall and stout like pipe cleaners. Roboto Slab follows with open-throated a, c, e and s, though shrinking Cabin Sketch would crowd those thick strokes.
gen-gf-cactus-classical-serif-fs-bespoke: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space where its curves meet the stem, so lines feel unhurried. Cactus Classical Serif above it adds gentle stroke variation and a friendly g.
gen-gf-caladea-fs-bespoke-sans: Bookish dignity up top, crisp lines below. Caladea shows only a modest gap between stems and hairlines, and Bespoke Sans keeps almost no contrast at all.
gen-gf-cantata-one-fs-bespoke-sans: Classic in manner, Cantata One spreads its letters in a loose row, with heavy verticals and thread-thin diagonals. And Bespoke Sans, with generous space at its curve ends, keeps paragraphs moving smoothly underneath.
gen-gf-capriola-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with sturdy thin lines and open curves. Capriola, plain and approachable above it, gives that richer text a straightforward front door.
gen-gf-chathura-fs-literata: Chathura compresses its letters into a quick cadence with barely a pause, outlined in one steady thickness. But Literata, a classic serif, slows things down, its thin strokes sitting close to its thick ones.
